    79→	// PendingPromptAttribution holds attribution calculated at prompt start (before agent runs).

    84→// PromptAttribution captures line-level attribution data at the start of each prompt.
    85→// By recording what changed since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent works,
    86→// we can accurately separate user edits from agent contributions.
    87→type PromptAttribution struct {
    88→	// CheckpointNumber is which checkpoint this was recorded before (1-indexed)
    89→	CheckpointNumber int `json:"checkpoint_number"`
    90→

    96→

    98→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
    99→	AgentLinesAdded int `json:"agent_lines_added"`
   100→
   101→	// AgentLinesRemoved is total agent lines removed so far (base → last checkpoint).
   102→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
   103→	AgentLinesRemoved int `json:"agent_lines_removed"`
   104→
   105→	// UserAddedPerFile tracks per-file user additions for accurate modification tracking.
   106→	// This enables distinguishing user self-modifications from agent modifications.
   107→	// See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details.
   108→	UserAddedPerFile map[string]int `json:"user_added_per_file,omitempty"`
   109→}
   110→
   111→// StateStore provides low-level operations for managing session state files.
   112→//
   113→// StateStore is a primitive for session state persistence. It is NOT the same as
   114→// the Sessions interface - it only handles state files in .git/entire-sessions/,
   115→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.
   116→//
   117→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
   118→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.
   119→type StateStore struct {
   120→	// stateDir is the directory where session state files are stored
   121→	stateDir string
   122→}
   123→
   124→// NewStateStore creates a new state store.
   125→// Uses the git common dir to store session state (shared across worktrees).
   126→func NewStateStore() (*StateStore, error) {
   127→	commonDir, err := getGitCommonDir()
   128→	if err != nil {
   129→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   130→	}
   131→	return &StateStore{
   132→		stateDir: filepath.Join(commonDir, sessionStateDirName),
   133→	}, nil
   134→}
   135→
   136→// NewStateStoreWithDir creates a new state store with a custom directory.
   137→// This is useful for testing.
   138→func NewStateStoreWithDir(stateDir string) *StateStore {
   139→	return &StateStore{stateDir: stateDir}
   140→}
   141→
   142→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   143→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   144→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   145→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   146→
   147→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   148→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   149→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   150→	}
   151→
   152→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   153→
   154→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   155→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   156→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   157→	}
   158→	if err != nil {
   159→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   160→	}
   161→
   162→	var state State
   163→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   164→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   165→	}
   166→	return &state, nil
   167→}
   168→
   169→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   170→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   171→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   172→
   173→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   174→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   175→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   176→	}
   177→
   178→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   179→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   180→	}
   181→
   182→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   183→	if err != nil {
   184→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   188→
   189→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   190→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   191→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   192→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   193→	}
   194→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   195→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   196→	}
   197→	return nil
   198→}
   199→
   200→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   201→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   202→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   203→
   204→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   205→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   206→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   207→	}
   208→
   209→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   210→
   211→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   212→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   213→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   214→		}
   215→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   216→	}
   217→	return nil
   218→}
   219→
   220→// RemoveAll removes the entire session state directory.
   221→// This is used during uninstall to completely remove all session state.
   222→func (s *StateStore) RemoveAll() error {
   223→	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.stateDir); err != nil {
   224→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state directory: %w", err)
   225→	}
   226→	return nil
   227→}
   228→
   229→// List returns all session states.
   230→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   231→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   232→
   233→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   234→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   235→		return nil, nil
   236→	}
   237→	if err != nil {
   238→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	var states []*State
   242→	for _, entry := range entries {
   243→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   244→			continue
   245→		}
   246→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   247→			continue // Skip temp files
   248→		}
   249→
   250→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   251→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   252→		if err != nil {
   253→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   254→		}
   255→		if state == nil {
   256→			continue
   257→		}
   258→
   259→		states = append(states, state)
   260→	}
   261→	return states, nil
   262→}
   263→
   264→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   265→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   266→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   267→}
   268→
   269→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   270→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   271→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   272→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   273→	ctx := context.Background()
   274→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   275→	cmd.Dir = "."
   276→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   277→	if err != nil {
   278→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   282→
   283→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   284→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   285→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   286→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   287→	}
   288→
   289→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   290→}

Contains:

- **`(p Phase) IsActive() bool`** -- returns true for `PhaseActive` and `PhaseActiveCommitted`
- **`Event` type** (int enum with iota): `EventUserPromptSubmit`, `EventStop`, `EventGitCommit`, `EventSessionStart`, `EventSessionStop`
- **`Action` type** (int enum with iota): `ActionCondense`, `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched`, `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles`, `ActionMigrateShadowBranch`, `ActionWarnStaleSession`, `ActionClearEndedAt`, `ActionUpdateLastInteraction`

- **`TransitionResult` struct**: `NewPhase Phase`, `Actions []Action`
- **`Transition()` function** -- pure function implementing the full transition table. Normalizes empty/unknown phase to `PhaseIdle` at the top, then dispatches to per-phase helper functions (`transitionFromIdle`, `transitionFromActive`, `transitionFromActiveCommitted`, `transitionFromEnded`) each with exhaustive event switch statements and default cases
- **`MermaidDiagram()` function** -- generates a Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` by iterating all (Phase, Event, TransitionContext) combinations, calling `Transition()`, and formatting the results. Always in sync with implementation since it is derived from the actual function.

**`/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/1/cmd/entire/cli/session/phase_test.go`** -- Exhaustive tests (437 lines)

Contains:
- **`TestPhaseFromString`** -- 7 cases including empty, unknown, uppercase
- **`TestPhase_IsActive`** -- 4 cases for all phases
- **`TestEvent_String`** -- 5 cases for all events
- **`TestAction_String`** -- 7 cases for all actions
- **`TestTransition`** -- 31 table-driven test cases covering:
  - All IDLE transitions (6 cases including rebase)
  - All ACTIVE transitions (6 cases including rebase)
  - All ACTIVE_COMMITTED transitions (6 cases including rebase)
  - All ENDED transitions (7 cases including rebase, files/no-files)
  - Empty phase backward compat (5 cases: one per event)
  - Unknown phase backward compat (1 case)
- **`TestTransition_rebase_always_produces_empty_actions`** -- verifies rebase produces empty actions AND preserves phase for all 4 phases
- **`TestTransition_all_phase_event_combinations_are_defined`** -- verifies no panics and canonical phases for all 20 (4 phases x 5 events) combinations

### Verification Results

- `mise run fmt` -- clean, no formatting changes needed
- `golangci-lint run ./cmd/entire/cli/session/... --new=false` -- 0 issues
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/session/...` -- all tests pass
- `mise run test` -- full test suite passes (21 packages, 0 failures)

### Design Decisions

1. **Per-phase helper functions** instead of a single nested switch -- keeps each function focused and under the complexity threshold, while still having exhaustive event coverage with default cases for the linter.

2. **`allPhases` and `allEvents` package-level slices** -- shared between production code (`MermaidDiagram()`) and tests (`TestTransition_rebase_always_produces_empty_actions`, `TestTransition_all_phase_event_combinations_are_defined`), ensuring coverage stays in sync when new phases/events are added.

3. **Nil vs empty slice for Actions** -- transitions with no actions return a `TransitionResult` with `Actions` field at zero value (`nil`), not `[]Action{}`. Tests assert `nil` for no-op cases to be precise about the semantics.

     8→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
     9→type Phase string
    10→
    11→const (

    13→	PhaseActiveCommitted Phase = "active_committed"
    14→	PhaseIdle            Phase = "idle"

    20→
    21→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty or unknown values
    22→// as PhaseIdle for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
    23→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
    24→	switch Phase(s) {
    25→	case PhaseActive:
    26→		return PhaseActive
    27→	case PhaseActiveCommitted:
    28→		return PhaseActiveCommitted
    29→	case PhaseIdle:
    30→		return PhaseIdle
    31→	case PhaseEnded:
    32→		return PhaseEnded
    33→	default:
    34→		return PhaseIdle
    35→	}
    36→}
    37→
    38→// IsActive reports whether the phase represents an active agent turn.
    39→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
    40→	return p == PhaseActive || p == PhaseActiveCommitted
    41→}
    42→
    43→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
    44→type Event int
    45→
    46→const (
    47→	EventUserPromptSubmit Event = iota // Agent received a new user prompt
    48→	EventStop                          // Agent turn ended (Stop hook)
    49→	EventGitCommit                     // A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
    50→	EventSessionStart                  // Session process started (SessionStart hook)
    51→	EventSessionStop                   // Session process ended (SessionStop hook)
    52→)

    54→// allEvents is the canonical list of events for enumeration.
    55→var allEvents = []Event{EventUserPromptSubmit, EventStop, EventGitCommit, EventSessionStart, EventSessionStop}
    56→
    57→// String returns a human-readable name for the event.
    58→func (e Event) String() string {
    59→	switch e {
    60→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
    61→		return "UserPromptSubmit"
    62→	case EventStop:
    63→		return "Stop"
    64→	case EventGitCommit:
    65→		return "GitCommit"
    66→	case EventSessionStart:
    67→		return "SessionStart"
    68→	case EventSessionStop:

    70→	default:
    71→		return fmt.Sprintf("Event(%d)", int(e))
    72→	}
    73→}
    74→
    75→// Action represents a side effect that should be performed after a transition.
    76→// The caller is responsible for executing these -- the state machine only declares them.
    77→type Action int
    78→
    79→const (
    80→	ActionCondense               Action = iota // Condense session data to permanent storage
    81→	ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched               // Condense only if FilesTouched is non-empty
    82→	ActionDiscardIfNoFiles                     // Discard session if FilesTouched is empty
    83→	ActionMigrateShadowBranch                  // Migrate shadow branch to new HEAD
    84→	ActionWarnStaleSession                     // Warn user about stale session(s)
    85→	ActionClearEndedAt                         // Clear EndedAt timestamp (session re-entering)
    86→	ActionUpdateLastInteraction                // Update LastInteractionTime
    87→)
    88→
    89→// String returns a human-readable name for the action.
    90→func (a Action) String() string {
    91→	switch a {
    92→	case ActionCondense:
    93→		return "Condense"
    94→	case ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
    95→		return "CondenseIfFilesTouched"
    96→	case ActionDiscardIfNoFiles:
    97→		return "DiscardIfNoFiles"
    98→	case ActionMigrateShadowBranch:
    99→		return "MigrateShadowBranch"
   100→	case ActionWarnStaleSession:
   101→		return "WarnStaleSession"
   102→	case ActionClearEndedAt:
   103→		return "ClearEndedAt"
   104→	case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:
   105→		return "UpdateLastInteraction"
   106→	default:
   107→		return fmt.Sprintf("Action(%d)", int(a))
   108→	}
   109→}
   110→
   111→// TransitionContext provides read-only context for transitions that need
   112→// to inspect session state without mutating it.
   113→type TransitionContext struct {
   114→	HasFilesTouched    bool // len(FilesTouched) > 0
   115→	IsRebaseInProgress bool // .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ exists
   116→}
   117→
   118→// TransitionResult holds the outcome of a state machine transition.
   119→type TransitionResult struct {
   120→	NewPhase Phase
   121→	Actions  []Action
   122→}
   123→
   124→// Transition computes the next phase and required actions given the current
   125→// phase and an event. This is a pure function with no side effects.
   126→//
   127→// Empty or unknown phase values are normalized to PhaseIdle for backward
   128→// compatibility with session state files created before phase tracking.
   129→func Transition(current Phase, event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   130→	// Normalize empty/unknown phase to idle for backward compatibility.
   131→	current = PhaseFromString(string(current))
   132→
   133→	switch current {
   134→	case PhaseIdle:
   135→		return transitionFromIdle(event, ctx)
   136→	case PhaseActive:
   137→		return transitionFromActive(event, ctx)
   138→	case PhaseActiveCommitted:
   139→		return transitionFromActiveCommitted(event, ctx)
   140→	case PhaseEnded:
   141→		return transitionFromEnded(event, ctx)
   142→	default:
   143→		// PhaseFromString guarantees we only get known phases, but the
   144→		// exhaustive linter requires handling the default case.
   145→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   146→	}
   147→}
   148→
   149→func transitionFromIdle(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   150→	switch event {
   151→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   152→		return TransitionResult{
   153→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   154→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   155→		}
   156→	case EventStop:
   157→		// Stop while idle is a no-op (no active turn to end).
   158→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   159→	case EventGitCommit:
   160→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   161→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   162→		}
   163→		return TransitionResult{
   164→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   165→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   166→		}
   167→	case EventSessionStart:
   168→		// Already condensable, no-op.
   169→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   170→	case EventSessionStop:
   171→		return TransitionResult{
   172→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   173→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   174→		}
   175→	default:
   176→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   177→	}
   178→}
   179→
   180→func transitionFromActive(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   181→	switch event {
   182→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   183→		// Ctrl-C recovery: just continue.
   184→		return TransitionResult{
   185→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   186→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   187→		}
   188→	case EventStop:
   189→		return TransitionResult{
   190→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   191→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   192→		}
   193→	case EventGitCommit:
   194→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   195→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   196→		}
   197→		return TransitionResult{
   198→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   199→			Actions:  []Action{ActionMigrateShadowBranch, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   200→		}
   201→	case EventSessionStart:
   202→		return TransitionResult{
   203→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   204→			Actions:  []Action{ActionWarnStaleSession},
   205→		}
   206→	case EventSessionStop:
   207→		return TransitionResult{
   208→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   209→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   210→		}
   211→	default:
   212→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   213→	}
   214→}
   215→
   216→func transitionFromActiveCommitted(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   217→	switch event {
   218→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   219→		// Ctrl-C recovery after commit.
   220→		return TransitionResult{
   221→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   222→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   223→		}
   224→	case EventStop:
   225→		return TransitionResult{
   226→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   227→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   228→		}
   229→	case EventGitCommit:
   230→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   231→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted}
   232→		}
   233→		return TransitionResult{
   234→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   235→			Actions:  []Action{ActionMigrateShadowBranch, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   236→		}
   237→	case EventSessionStart:
   238→		return TransitionResult{
   239→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   240→			Actions:  []Action{ActionWarnStaleSession},
   241→		}
   242→	case EventSessionStop:
   243→		return TransitionResult{
   244→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   245→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   246→		}
   247→	default:
   248→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted}
   249→	}
   250→}
   251→
   252→func transitionFromEnded(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   253→	switch event {
   254→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   255→		return TransitionResult{
   256→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   257→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   258→		}
   259→	case EventStop:
   260→		// Stop while ended is a no-op.
   261→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   262→	case EventGitCommit:
   263→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   264→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   265→		}
   266→		if ctx.HasFilesTouched {
   267→			return TransitionResult{
   268→				NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   269→				Actions:  []Action{ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   270→			}
   271→		}
   272→		return TransitionResult{
   273→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   274→			Actions:  []Action{ActionDiscardIfNoFiles, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   275→		}
   276→	case EventSessionStart:
   277→		return TransitionResult{
   278→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   279→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt},
   280→		}
   281→	case EventSessionStop:
   282→		// Already ended, no-op.
   283→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   284→	default:
   285→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   286→	}
   287→}
   288→
   289→// MermaidDiagram generates a Mermaid state diagram from the transition table.
   290→// The diagram is derived by calling Transition() for all (phase, event, context)
   291→// combinations, so it is always in sync with the implementation.
   292→func MermaidDiagram() string {
   293→	var b strings.Builder
   294→	b.WriteString("stateDiagram-v2\n")
   295→
   296→	// State declarations with descriptions.
   297→	b.WriteString("    state \"IDLE\" as idle\n")
   298→	b.WriteString("    state \"ACTIVE\" as active\n")
   299→	b.WriteString("    state \"ACTIVE_COMMITTED\" as active_committed\n")
   300→	b.WriteString("    state \"ENDED\" as ended\n")
   301→	b.WriteString("\n")
   302→
   303→	// Context variants for GitCommit: rebase, files/no-files.
   304→	type contextVariant struct {
   305→		label string
   306→		ctx   TransitionContext
   307→	}
   308→
   309→	// For each phase/event, generate edges.
   310→	for _, phase := range allPhases {
   311→		for _, event := range allEvents {
   312→			var variants []contextVariant
   313→			if event == EventGitCommit {
   314→				variants = []contextVariant{
   315→					{"", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: true, IsRebaseInProgress: false}},
   316→					{"[no files]", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: false, IsRebaseInProgress: false}},
   317→					{"[rebase]", TransitionContext{IsRebaseInProgress: true}},
   318→				}
   319→			} else {
   320→				variants = []contextVariant{
   321→					{"", TransitionContext{}},
   322→				}
   323→			}
   324→
   325→			for _, v := range variants {
   326→				result := Transition(phase, event, v.ctx)
   327→
   328→				// Build edge label.
   329→				label := event.String()
   330→				if v.label != "" {
   331→					label += " " + v.label
   332→				}
   333→				if len(result.Actions) > 0 {
   334→					actionNames := make([]string, 0, len(result.Actions))
   335→					for _, a := range result.Actions {
   336→						actionNames = append(actionNames, a.String())
   337→					}
   338→					label += " / " + strings.Join(actionNames, ", ")
   339→				}
   340→
   341→				from := string(phase)
   342→				to := string(result.NewPhase)
   343→
   344→				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s --> %s : %s\n", from, to, label)
   345→			}
   346→		}
   347→	}
   348→
   349→	return b.String()
   350→}
   351→

### 2. `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/1/cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers_test.go`

**Pattern:** Multiple assertions per test case

### 3. `/Users/alex/workspace/cli/.worktrees/1/cmd/entire/cli/validation/validators_test.go`

**Pattern:** Boolean error checking with conditional message validation
```go
if tt.wantErr {
    if err == nil {
        t.Errorf("ValidateXXX(%q) expected error containing %q, got nil", value, tt.errMsg)
        return
    }
    if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.errMsg) {
        t.Errorf("ValidateXXX(%q) error = %q, want error containing %q", value, err.Error(), tt.errMsg)
    }
} else if err != nil {
    t.Errorf("ValidateXXX(%q) unexpected error: %v", value, err)
}
```

**Example (Line 74-84):**

err := ValidateSessionID(tt.sessionID)

    if err == nil {
        t.Errorf("ValidateSessionID(%q) expected error containing %q, got nil", tt.sessionID, tt.errMsg)
        return
    }
    if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.errMsg) {
        t.Errorf("ValidateSessionID(%q) error = %q, want error containing %q", tt.sessionID, err.Error(), tt.errMsg)
    }

    t.Errorf("ValidateSessionID(%q) unexpected error: %v", tt.sessionID, err)

## Summary

The codebase uses **straightforward assertions**:

1. **Simple equality**: `if got != tt.want` with `t.Errorf()`
2. **Multiple fields**: Each field checked separately with its own conditional
3. **Error validation**: Boolean `wantErr` flag with nested error message validation using `strings.Contains()`

All errors are reported using **`t.Errorf()`** with descriptive format strings that show function name, input, actual result, and expected result.

    49→// PromptAttribution captures line-level attribution data at the start of each prompt,
    50→// calculated BEFORE the agent runs. This allows us to separate user edits (made between
    51→// prompts) from agent edits (made during prompt execution).
    52→//
    53→// Fields:
    54→//   - CheckpointNumber: Which checkpoint this attribution is for (1-indexed)
    55→//   - UserLinesAdded/Removed: User edits since the last checkpoint (lastCheckpoint → worktree)
    56→//   - AgentLinesAdded/Removed: Cumulative agent work so far (base → lastCheckpoint)
    57→//   - UserAddedPerFile: Per-file breakdown of user additions (for accurate modification tracking)
    58→//
    59→// Note: For checkpoint 1, AgentLinesAdded/Removed are always 0 because there is no previous
    60→// checkpoint to compare against. This doesn't mean the agent hasn't done work yet - it means
    61→// we can't measure cumulative agent work until after the first checkpoint is created.
    62→// These fields become meaningful starting from checkpoint 2.
    63→//
    64→// UserAddedPerFile enables accurate tracking of user self-modifications. When a user modifies
    65→// their own previously-added lines (not agent lines), we shouldn't subtract from the agent's
    66→// contribution. See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details.
    67→type PromptAttribution struct {
    68→	CheckpointNumber  int            `json:"checkpoint_number"`
    69→	UserLinesAdded    int            `json:"user_lines_added"`
    70→	UserLinesRemoved  int            `json:"user_lines_removed"`
    71→	AgentLinesAdded   int            `json:"agent_lines_added"`             // Always 0 for checkpoint 1 (no previous checkpoint)
    72→	AgentLinesRemoved int            `json:"agent_lines_removed"`           // Always 0 for checkpoint 1 (no previous checkpoint)
    73→	UserAddedPerFile  map[string]int `json:"user_added_per_file,omitempty"` // Per-file user additions for modification tracking
    74→}

    78→type CheckpointInfo struct {

    80→	SessionID        string          `json:"session_id"`

    16→// Shadow strategy session state methods.
    17→// Uses session.StateStore for persistence.

    19→// loadSessionState loads session state using the StateStore.
    20→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) loadSessionState(sessionID string) (*SessionState, error) {
    21→	store, err := s.getStateStore()
    22→	if err != nil {
    23→		return nil, err
    24→	}
    25→	state, err := store.Load(context.Background(), sessionID)
    26→	if err != nil {
    27→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
    28→	}
    29→	return sessionStateToStrategy(state), nil
    30→}
    31→
    32→// saveSessionState saves session state using the StateStore.
    33→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) saveSessionState(state *SessionState) error {
    34→	store, err := s.getStateStore()
    35→	if err != nil {
    36→		return err
    37→	}
    38→	if err := store.Save(context.Background(), sessionStateFromStrategy(state)); err != nil {
    39→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
    40→	}
    41→	return nil
    42→}
    43→
    44→// clearSessionState clears session state using the StateStore.
    45→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) clearSessionState(sessionID string) error {
    46→	store, err := s.getStateStore()
    47→	if err != nil {
    48→		return err
    49→	}
    50→	if err := store.Clear(context.Background(), sessionID); err != nil {
    51→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
    52→	}
    53→	return nil
    54→}
    55→
    56→// listAllSessionStates returns all active session states.
    57→// It filters out orphaned sessions whose shadow branch no longer exists.
    58→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) listAllSessionStates() ([]*SessionState, error) {
    59→	store, err := s.getStateStore()
    60→	if err != nil {
    61→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get state store: %w", err)
    62→	}
    63→
    64→	sessionStates, err := store.List(context.Background())
    65→	if err != nil {
    66→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list session states: %w", err)
    67→	}
    68→
    69→	if len(sessionStates) == 0 {
    70→		return nil, nil
    71→	}
    72→
    73→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
    74→	if err != nil {
    75→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
    76→	}
    77→
    78→	var states []*SessionState
    79→	for _, sessionState := range sessionStates {
    80→		state := sessionStateToStrategy(sessionState)
    81→
    82→		// Skip and cleanup orphaned sessions whose shadow branch no longer exists
    83→		// Only cleanup if the session has created checkpoints (CheckpointCount > 0)
    84→		// AND has no LastCheckpointID (not recently condensed)
    85→		// Sessions with LastCheckpointID are valid - they were condensed and the shadow
    86→		// branch was intentionally deleted. Keep them for LastCheckpointID reuse.
    87→		shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
    88→		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
    89→		if _, err := repo.Reference(refName, true); err != nil {
    90→			// Shadow branch doesn't exist
    91→			// Only cleanup if session has checkpoints AND no LastCheckpointID
    92→			// Sessions with LastCheckpointID should be kept for checkpoint reuse
    93→			if state.CheckpointCount > 0 && state.LastCheckpointID == "" {
    94→				// Clear the orphaned session state (best-effort, don't fail listing)
    95→				//nolint:errcheck,gosec // G104: Cleanup is best-effort, shouldn't fail the list operation
    96→				store.Clear(context.Background(), state.SessionID)
    97→				continue
    98→			}
    99→			// Keep sessions with LastCheckpointID or no checkpoints yet
   100→		}
   101→
   102→		states = append(states, state)
   103→	}
   104→	return states, nil
   105→}

   107→// findSessionsForWorktree finds all sessions for the given worktree path.
   108→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath string) ([]*SessionState, error) {
   109→	allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates()
   110→	if err != nil {
   111→		return nil, err
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	var matching []*SessionState
   115→	for _, state := range allStates {
   116→		if state.WorktreePath == worktreePath {
   117→			matching = append(matching, state)
   118→		}
   119→	}
   120→	return matching, nil
   121→}
   122→
   123→// findSessionsForCommit finds all sessions where base_commit matches the given SHA.
   124→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) findSessionsForCommit(baseCommitSHA string) ([]*SessionState, error) {
   125→	allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates()
   126→	if err != nil {
   127→		return nil, err
   128→	}
   129→
   130→	var matching []*SessionState
   131→	for _, state := range allStates {
   132→		if state.BaseCommit == baseCommitSHA {
   133→			matching = append(matching, state)
   134→		}
   135→	}
   136→	return matching, nil
   137→}
   138→
   139→// FindSessionsForCommit is the exported version of findSessionsForCommit.
   140→// Used by the rewind reset command to find sessions to clean up.
   141→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) FindSessionsForCommit(baseCommitSHA string) ([]*SessionState, error) {
   142→	return s.findSessionsForCommit(baseCommitSHA)
   143→}
   144→
   145→// ClearSessionState is the exported version of clearSessionState.
   146→// Used by the rewind reset command to clean up session state files.
   147→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) ClearSessionState(sessionID string) error {
   148→	return s.clearSessionState(sessionID)
   149→}
   150→
   151→// CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints counts how many other active sessions
   152→// from the SAME worktree (different from currentSessionID) have created checkpoints
   153→// on the SAME base commit (current HEAD). This is used to show an informational message
   154→// about concurrent sessions that will be included in the next commit.
   155→// Returns 0, nil if no such sessions exist.
   156→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(currentSessionID string) (int, error) {
   157→	currentWorktree, err := GetWorktreePath()
   158→	if err != nil {
   159→		return 0, err
   160→	}
   161→
   162→	// Get current HEAD to compare with session base commits
   163→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   164→	if err != nil {
   165→		return 0, err
   166→	}
   167→	head, err := repo.Head()
   168→	if err != nil {
   169→		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   170→	}
   171→	currentHead := head.Hash().String()
   172→
   173→	allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates()
   174→	if err != nil {
   175→		return 0, err
   176→	}
   177→
   178→	count := 0
   179→	for _, state := range allStates {
   180→		// Only consider sessions from the same worktree with checkpoints
   181→		// AND based on the same commit (current HEAD)
   182→		// Sessions from different base commits are independent and shouldn't be counted
   183→		if state.SessionID != currentSessionID &&
   184→			state.WorktreePath == currentWorktree &&
   185→			state.CheckpointCount > 0 &&
   186→			state.BaseCommit == currentHead {
   187→			count++
   188→		}
   189→	}
   190→	return count, nil
   191→}
   192→
   193→// initializeSession creates a new session state or updates a partial one.
   194→// A partial state may exist if the concurrent session warning was shown.
   195→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
   196→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
   197→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) initializeSession(repo *git.Repository, sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string) (*SessionState, error) {
   198→	head, err := repo.Head()
   199→	if err != nil {
   200→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   204→	if err != nil {
   205→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree path: %w", err)
   206→	}
   207→
   208→	// Get worktree ID for shadow branch naming
   209→	worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
   210→	if err != nil {
   211→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree ID: %w", err)
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// Capture untracked files at session start to preserve them during rewind
   215→	untrackedFiles, err := collectUntrackedFiles()
   216→	if err != nil {
   217→		// Non-fatal: continue even if we can't collect untracked files
   218→		untrackedFiles = nil
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	state := &SessionState{
   222→		SessionID:             sessionID,
   223→		BaseCommit:            head.Hash().String(),
   224→		WorktreePath:          worktreePath,
   225→		WorktreeID:            worktreeID,
   226→		StartedAt:             time.Now(),
   227→		CheckpointCount:       0,
   228→		UntrackedFilesAtStart: untrackedFiles,
   229→		AgentType:             agentType,
   230→		TranscriptPath:        transcriptPath,
   231→	}
   232→
   233→	if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   234→		return nil, err
   235→	}
   236→
   237→	return state, nil
   238→}

   241→// worktreeID should be empty for the main worktree or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   242→func getShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID string) string {
   243→	return checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID)
   244→}

Now let me find the converter functions that map between `session.State` and `strategy.SessionState`.

> DEVELOPER

still reviewing. 

These events - tested by TestEvent_String - are we binding too hard to Claude here? I actually prefer the gemini AfterAgent or something like 'AgentFinishesTurn' <- not this but something like it 😅

> AGENT

Good catch. `EventStop` and `EventUserPromptSubmit` are literally Claude Code hook names. The state machine should be agent-agnostic — it describes *what happened*, not *which hook fired*.

How about:

| Current | Proposed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `EventUserPromptSubmit` | `EventTurnStart` | Agent begins working on a prompt |
| `EventStop` | `EventTurnEnd` | Agent finishes its turn |
| `EventGitCommit` | `EventGitCommit` | (already generic) |
| `EventSessionStart` | `EventSessionStart` | (already generic) |
| `EventSessionStop` | `EventSessionStop` | (already generic) |

`TurnStart`/`TurnEnd` describes the semantic lifecycle without binding to any agent's hook vocabulary. The mapping from Claude's `UserPromptSubmit` → `EventTurnStart` or Gemini's `AfterAgent` → `EventTurnEnd` happens in the hook handler layer, not in the state machine.

> DEVELOPER

is 'Turn' a good word? I guess in the subagent case the 'user' prompt is a misnomer

> AGENT

"Turn" is good. It's the standard term in conversational/agent systems for one cycle of "receive input → process → produce output" — regardless of whether the input came from a human or a parent agent. It doesn't imply who the sender is.

Quick check it doesn't collide with our terminology:
- **Checkpoint** = permanent data on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- **Step** = shadow branch commit (rewind point)
- **Turn** = one cycle of agent work (prompt received → agent works → agent done)

A turn may produce zero or one steps. Multiple turns happen between checkpoints. No overlap.

Want me to rename `EventUserPromptSubmit` → `EventTurnStart` and `EventStop` → `EventTurnEnd` in `phase.go` and `phase_test.go`?

     1→package session

     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"

     7→
     8→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
     9→type Phase string
    10→
    11→const (
    12→	PhaseActive          Phase = "active"
    13→	PhaseActiveCommitted Phase = "active_committed"
    14→	PhaseIdle            Phase = "idle"
    15→	PhaseEnded           Phase = "ended"
    16→)
    17→
    18→// allPhases is the canonical list of phases for enumeration (e.g., diagram generation).
    19→var allPhases = []Phase{PhaseIdle, PhaseActive, PhaseActiveCommitted, PhaseEnded}
    20→
    21→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty or unknown values
    22→// as PhaseIdle for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
    23→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
    24→	switch Phase(s) {
    25→	case PhaseActive:
    26→		return PhaseActive
    27→	case PhaseActiveCommitted:
    28→		return PhaseActiveCommitted
    29→	case PhaseIdle:
    30→		return PhaseIdle
    31→	case PhaseEnded:
    32→		return PhaseEnded
    33→	default:
    34→		return PhaseIdle
    35→	}
    36→}
    37→
    38→// IsActive reports whether the phase represents an active agent turn.
    39→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
    40→	return p == PhaseActive || p == PhaseActiveCommitted
    41→}
    42→
    43→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
    44→type Event int
    45→
    46→const (
    47→	EventUserPromptSubmit Event = iota // Agent received a new user prompt
    48→	EventStop                          // Agent turn ended (Stop hook)
    49→	EventGitCommit                     // A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
    50→	EventSessionStart                  // Session process started (SessionStart hook)
    51→	EventSessionStop                   // Session process ended (SessionStop hook)
    52→)
    53→
    54→// allEvents is the canonical list of events for enumeration.
    55→var allEvents = []Event{EventUserPromptSubmit, EventStop, EventGitCommit, EventSessionStart, EventSessionStop}
    56→
    57→// String returns a human-readable name for the event.
    58→func (e Event) String() string {
    59→	switch e {
    60→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
    61→		return "UserPromptSubmit"
    62→	case EventStop:
    63→		return "Stop"
    64→	case EventGitCommit:
    65→		return "GitCommit"
    66→	case EventSessionStart:
    67→		return "SessionStart"
    68→	case EventSessionStop:
    69→		return "SessionStop"
    70→	default:
    71→		return fmt.Sprintf("Event(%d)", int(e))
    72→	}
    73→}
    74→
    75→// Action represents a side effect that should be performed after a transition.
    76→// The caller is responsible for executing these -- the state machine only declares them.
    77→type Action int
    78→
    79→const (
    80→	ActionCondense               Action = iota // Condense session data to permanent storage
    81→	ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched               // Condense only if FilesTouched is non-empty
    82→	ActionDiscardIfNoFiles                     // Discard session if FilesTouched is empty
    83→	ActionMigrateShadowBranch                  // Migrate shadow branch to new HEAD
    84→	ActionWarnStaleSession                     // Warn user about stale session(s)
    85→	ActionClearEndedAt                         // Clear EndedAt timestamp (session re-entering)
    86→	ActionUpdateLastInteraction                // Update LastInteractionTime
    87→)
    88→
    89→// String returns a human-readable name for the action.
    90→func (a Action) String() string {
    91→	switch a {
    92→	case ActionCondense:
    93→		return "Condense"
    94→	case ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
    95→		return "CondenseIfFilesTouched"
    96→	case ActionDiscardIfNoFiles:
    97→		return "DiscardIfNoFiles"
    98→	case ActionMigrateShadowBranch:
    99→		return "MigrateShadowBranch"
   100→	case ActionWarnStaleSession:
   101→		return "WarnStaleSession"
   102→	case ActionClearEndedAt:
   103→		return "ClearEndedAt"
   104→	case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:

   111→// TransitionContext provides read-only context for transitions that need

   117→
   118→// TransitionResult holds the outcome of a state machine transition.
   119→type TransitionResult struct {
   120→	NewPhase Phase
   121→	Actions  []Action
   122→}
   123→
   124→// Transition computes the next phase and required actions given the current
   125→// phase and an event. This is a pure function with no side effects.
   126→//
   127→// Empty or unknown phase values are normalized to PhaseIdle for backward
   128→// compatibility with session state files created before phase tracking.
   129→func Transition(current Phase, event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   130→	// Normalize empty/unknown phase to idle for backward compatibility.
   131→	current = PhaseFromString(string(current))
   132→
   133→	switch current {
   134→	case PhaseIdle:
   135→		return transitionFromIdle(event, ctx)
   136→	case PhaseActive:
   137→		return transitionFromActive(event, ctx)
   138→	case PhaseActiveCommitted:
   139→		return transitionFromActiveCommitted(event, ctx)
   140→	case PhaseEnded:
   141→		return transitionFromEnded(event, ctx)
   142→	default:
   143→		// PhaseFromString guarantees we only get known phases, but the
   144→		// exhaustive linter requires handling the default case.
   145→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   146→	}
   147→}
   148→
   149→func transitionFromIdle(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   150→	switch event {
   151→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   152→		return TransitionResult{
   153→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   154→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   155→		}
   156→	case EventStop:
   157→		// Stop while idle is a no-op (no active turn to end).
   158→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   159→	case EventGitCommit:
   160→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   161→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   162→		}
   163→		return TransitionResult{
   164→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   165→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   166→		}
   167→	case EventSessionStart:
   168→		// Already condensable, no-op.
   169→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   170→	case EventSessionStop:
   171→		return TransitionResult{
   172→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   173→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   174→		}
   175→	default:
   176→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   177→	}
   178→}
   179→
   180→func transitionFromActive(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   181→	switch event {
   182→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   183→		// Ctrl-C recovery: just continue.
   184→		return TransitionResult{
   185→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   186→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   187→		}
   188→	case EventStop:
   189→		return TransitionResult{
   190→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   191→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   192→		}
   193→	case EventGitCommit:
   194→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   195→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   196→		}
   197→		return TransitionResult{
   198→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   199→			Actions:  []Action{ActionMigrateShadowBranch, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   200→		}
   201→	case EventSessionStart:
   202→		return TransitionResult{
   203→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   204→			Actions:  []Action{ActionWarnStaleSession},
   205→		}
   206→	case EventSessionStop:
   207→		return TransitionResult{
   208→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   209→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   210→		}
   211→	default:
   212→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   213→	}
   214→}
   215→
   216→func transitionFromActiveCommitted(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   217→	switch event {
   218→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   219→		// Ctrl-C recovery after commit.
   220→		return TransitionResult{
   221→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   222→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   223→		}
   224→	case EventStop:
   225→		return TransitionResult{
   226→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   227→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   228→		}
   229→	case EventGitCommit:
   230→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   231→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted}
   232→		}
   233→		return TransitionResult{
   234→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   235→			Actions:  []Action{ActionMigrateShadowBranch, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   236→		}
   237→	case EventSessionStart:
   238→		return TransitionResult{
   239→			NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted,
   240→			Actions:  []Action{ActionWarnStaleSession},
   241→		}
   242→	case EventSessionStop:
   243→		return TransitionResult{
   244→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   245→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   246→		}
   247→	default:
   248→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActiveCommitted}
   249→	}
   250→}
   251→
   252→func transitionFromEnded(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   253→	switch event {
   254→	case EventUserPromptSubmit:
   255→		return TransitionResult{
   256→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   257→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   258→		}
   259→	case EventStop:
   260→		// Stop while ended is a no-op.
   261→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   262→	case EventGitCommit:
   263→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   264→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   265→		}
   266→		if ctx.HasFilesTouched {
   267→			return TransitionResult{
   268→				NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   269→				Actions:  []Action{ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   270→			}
   271→		}
   272→		return TransitionResult{
   273→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   274→			Actions:  []Action{ActionDiscardIfNoFiles, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   275→		}
   276→	case EventSessionStart:
   277→		return TransitionResult{
   278→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   279→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt},
   280→		}
   281→	case EventSessionStop:
   282→		// Already ended, no-op.
   283→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   284→	default:
   285→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   286→	}
   287→}
   288→
   289→// MermaidDiagram generates a Mermaid state diagram from the transition table.
   290→// The diagram is derived by calling Transition() for all (phase, event, context)
   291→// combinations, so it is always in sync with the implementation.
   292→func MermaidDiagram() string {
   293→	var b strings.Builder
   294→	b.WriteString("stateDiagram-v2\n")
   295→
   296→	// State declarations with descriptions.
   297→	b.WriteString("    state \"IDLE\" as idle\n")
   298→	b.WriteString("    state \"ACTIVE\" as active\n")
   299→	b.WriteString("    state \"ACTIVE_COMMITTED\" as active_committed\n")
   300→	b.WriteString("    state \"ENDED\" as ended\n")
   301→	b.WriteString("\n")
   302→
   303→	// Context variants for GitCommit: rebase, files/no-files.
   304→	type contextVariant struct {
   305→		label string
   306→		ctx   TransitionContext
   307→	}
   308→
   309→	// For each phase/event, generate edges.
   310→	for _, phase := range allPhases {
   311→		for _, event := range allEvents {
   312→			var variants []contextVariant
   313→			if event == EventGitCommit {
   314→				variants = []contextVariant{
   315→					{"", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: true, IsRebaseInProgress: false}},
   316→					{"[no files]", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: false, IsRebaseInProgress: false}},
   317→					{"[rebase]", TransitionContext{IsRebaseInProgress: true}},
   318→				}
   319→			} else {
   320→				variants = []contextVariant{
   321→					{"", TransitionContext{}},
   322→				}
   323→			}
   324→
   325→			for _, v := range variants {
   326→				result := Transition(phase, event, v.ctx)
   327→
   328→				// Build edge label.
   329→				label := event.String()
   330→				if v.label != "" {
   331→					label += " " + v.label
   332→				}
   333→				if len(result.Actions) > 0 {
   334→					actionNames := make([]string, 0, len(result.Actions))
   335→					for _, a := range result.Actions {
   336→						actionNames = append(actionNames, a.String())
   337→					}
   338→					label += " / " + strings.Join(actionNames, ", ")
   339→				}
   340→
   341→				from := string(phase)
   342→				to := string(result.NewPhase)
   343→
   344→				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s --> %s : %s\n", from, to, label)
   345→			}
   346→		}
   347→	}
   348→
   349→	return b.String()
   350→}
   351→

   358→	for _, tt := range tests {

   361→
   362→			result := Transition(tt.current, tt.event, tt.ctx)
   363→
   364→			assert.Equal(t, tt.wantPhase, result.NewPhase, "unexpected NewPhase")
   365→			assert.Equal(t, tt.wantActions, result.Actions, "unexpected Actions")
   366→		})
   367→	}
   368→}
   369→
   370→func TestTransition_rebase_always_produces_empty_actions(t *testing.T) {
   371→	t.Parallel()
   372→
   373→	rebaseCtx := TransitionContext{IsRebaseInProgress: true}
   374→
   375→	for _, phase := range allPhases {
   376→		result := Transition(phase, EventGitCommit, rebaseCtx)
   377→		assert.Empty(t, result.Actions,
   378→			"rebase should produce empty actions for phase %s", phase)
   379→		assert.Equal(t, phase, result.NewPhase,
   380→			"rebase should not change phase for %s", phase)
   381→	}
   382→}
   383→
   384→func TestTransition_all_phase_event_combinations_are_defined(t *testing.T) {
   385→	t.Parallel()
   386→
   387→	// Verify that calling Transition for every (phase, event) combination
   388→	// does not panic and returns a valid phase.
   389→	for _, phase := range allPhases {
   390→		for _, event := range allEvents {
   391→			result := Transition(phase, event, TransitionContext{})
   392→			assert.NotEmpty(t, string(result.NewPhase),
   393→				"Transition(%s, %s) returned empty phase", phase, event)
   394→
   395→			// Verify the resulting phase is a known phase.
   396→			normalized := PhaseFromString(string(result.NewPhase))
   397→			assert.Equal(t, result.NewPhase, normalized,
   398→				"Transition(%s, %s) returned non-canonical phase %q",
   399→				phase, event, result.NewPhase)
   400→		}
   401→	}
   402→}

     1→# ENT-221 + ENT-194: Session Phase State Machine (v2)
     2→
     3→> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.
     4→
     5→**Goal:** Introduce a session phase state machine so hooks can distinguish "agent committed mid-session" from "user committed between sessions", preventing premature condensation and data loss.
     6→
     7→**Architecture:** Add a Phase field to session state that tracks the session lifecycle (ACTIVE, ACTIVE_COMMITTED, IDLE, ENDED). Git hooks check the phase before deciding whether to condense.
     8→
     9→**Tech Stack:** Go, go-git v5
    10→
    11→**Supersedes:** `docs/plans/2026-02-06-session-phase-state-machine.md` (v1)
    12→**Review notes:** `docs/plans/2026-02-06-session-phase-review-notes.md`
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Terminology
    17→
    18→- **Checkpoint** = data condensed to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, linked to a user commit
    19→  via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Permanent storage. Created at commit time.
    20→- **Step** = shadow branch commit, one per SaveChanges (each agent turn). Rewindable.
    21→  Ephemeral until condensed into a checkpoint.
    22→
    23→A checkpoint may contain multiple steps' worth of data. The shadow branch accumulates
    24→steps until the user commits, at which point they are condensed into a checkpoint.
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→## Context
    29→
    30→When an AI agent commits via Bash mid-session (between UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks), `post-commit` fires and prematurely condenses session data, resets step count, and deletes the shadow branch. This causes:
    31→
    32→- **ENT-194**: Sequential agent commits produce empty/incomplete checkpoints because each `post-commit` condenses before the transcript is complete
    33→- **ENT-221**: No cross-hook state tracking means hooks can't distinguish "agent committed mid-session" from "user committed between sessions"
    34→
    35→The fix introduces a **session phase state machine** so hooks know the session's lifecycle stage.
    36→
    37→**Note:** File locking for concurrent hook access is deferred to ENT-238 (SQLite migration).
    38→The current atomic write-then-rename approach is retained, with a known narrow race window
    39→for concurrent hook processes.
    40→
    41→## State Machine
    42→
    43→### States
    44→
    45→| State | Description |
    46→|---|---|
    47→| **ACTIVE** | Agent is working on a turn. Set on UserPromptSubmit, cleared on Stop. |
    48→| **ACTIVE_COMMITTED** | Agent is working AND has made git commits this session. PostCommit defers condensation. |
    49→| **IDLE** | Turn finished, session still alive. Condensable on next user commit. |
    50→| **ENDED** | Session process exited. Condensable on next commit (if FilesTouched), otherwise discardable. |
    51→
    52→Note: UNINITIALIZED is not a stored state — it means no state file exists yet.
    53→Empty/missing Phase field in existing state files is treated as IDLE (backward compat).
    54→
    55→### Transitions
    56→
    57→```
    58→UNINITIALIZED ──UserPromptSubmit──────> ACTIVE           (state file created)
    59→ACTIVE ──Stop─────────────────────────> IDLE
    60→ACTIVE ──UserPromptSubmit─────────────> ACTIVE           (Ctrl-C recovery: just continue)
    61→ACTIVE ──git commit───────────────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    62→ACTIVE ──SessionStop──────────────────> ENDED            (graceful shutdown, no turn completed)
    63→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──git commit─────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    64→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──Stop───────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    65→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──SessionStop────────> ENDED            (agent died after committing)
    66→IDLE ──git commit─────────────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    67→IDLE ──UserPromptSubmit───────────────> ACTIVE
    68→IDLE ──SessionStop────────────────────> ENDED
    69→ENDED ──SessionStart (re-entry)───────> IDLE             (clear EndedAt, immediately condensable)
    70→ENDED ──git commit────────────────────> ENDED            ← triggers condense/discard action
    71→IDLE/ENDED ──UserPromptSubmit─────────> ACTIVE           (clear EndedAt if needed)
    72→```
    73→
    74→Condensation is an **action** triggered by certain transitions, not a state. The state
    75→machine declares `ActionCondense` (or `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` / `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles`)
    76→in the transition result; the caller executes it. See the transition table in Task 1 for
    77→the full action mapping.
    78→
    79→**SessionStart re-entry:** When `SessionStart` fires and a state file exists:
    80→- Phase = ENDED → set Phase = IDLE, clear EndedAt (session re-entered, immediately condensable)
    81→- Phase = IDLE → no-op (already condensable)
    82→- Phase = ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → leave as-is (warn user about stale session)
    83→- No state file → UNINITIALIZED (wait for UserPromptSubmit to create state)
    84→
    85→### Key Behaviors
    86→
    87→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED**: `post-commit` defers condensation, only updates BaseCommit + migrates shadow branch
    88→- **ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE**: Stop triggers immediate condensation (agent's commits already exist on branch)
    89→- **ACTIVE → ACTIVE (Ctrl-C recovery)**: Just reset to ACTIVE for new turn. No catch-up checkpoint. Interrupted turn's transcript data folds into next step naturally.
    90→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ENDED (SessionStop)**: Graceful shutdown without a completed turn. Shadow branch data preserved, condensable on next commit or via `entire sessions fix`.
    91→- **Shadow branch deletion**: Only when ALL sessions on the branch are condensed or discarded
    92→- **PendingCheckpointID**: Generated once per checkpoint cycle, shared across all commits in a session
    93→- **Rebase/merge detection**: PostCommit skips phase transitions during sequence operations (`.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` present)
    94→
    95→### Condensation Eligibility
    96→
    97→| Phase | FilesTouched? | Action |
    98→|---|---|---|
    99→| ACTIVE / IDLE | Any | **Condense** (session ongoing, context valuable) |
   100→| ENDED | Non-empty | **Condense** (contributed to code) |
   101→| ENDED | Empty | **Discard** (no code contribution, noise) |
   102→
   103→**Simplified rule:** Discard only when `ENDED AND len(FilesTouched) == 0`.
   104→
   105→Additionally, users can explicitly remove a session from checkpointing via `entire reset --session <id>`. This clears the session state; any file changes remain in the working directory for the user to handle via git.
   106→
   107→### Stale Session Detection
   108→
   109→No automatic timeout detection. Instead:
   110→
   111→- **SessionStart warning**: If other sessions exist with no interaction in ~hours, show:
   112→  `"Found N session(s) with no recent activity. Run 'entire sessions fix' to resolve."`
   113→- **`entire sessions fix`**: User-initiated command. Scans for sessions in pathological states
   114→  (ACTIVE_COMMITTED with no running agent, old ENDED sessions). Shows session info (phase,
   115→  last seen, shadow branch data). Lets user choose per session: Condense / Discard / Skip.
   116→- **`entire status`**: Enhanced to show session phases and stuck states.
   117→
   118→**Rationale:** TTL-based detection causes false positives (long builds, permission prompts,
   119→complex reasoning). Users can determine session liveness better than any heuristic.
   120→
   121→### `LastInteractionTime`
   122→
   123→Updated on **every hook invocation** — UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.
   124→Provides accurate "last seen" signal for the `entire sessions fix` UI and SessionStart warning.
   125→
   126→### Known Limitations
   127→
   128→**Ctrl-C interruption:** When a user Ctrl-C's during agent work, no hook fires. The session
   129→stays in ACTIVE. On next UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE → ACTIVE transition → just continue.
   130→The interrupted turn gets no rewind point (step), but its transcript lines fold into the next
   131→step. Files modified during the interrupted turn are captured via `git status` in subsequent
   132→steps, though without fine-grained transcript attribution.
   133→
   134→**ACTIVE_COMMITTED + dead agent:** If an agent commits mid-session and then crashes (no Stop
   135→hook fires), the session is stuck in ACTIVE_COMMITTED. PostCommit will always defer for this
   136→session. Resolution: user runs `entire sessions fix` to condense or discard. Data is safe on
   137→the shadow branch until resolved.
   138→
   139→**Backward compatibility:** Existing sessions without a Phase field are treated as IDLE
   140→(empty → IDLE). In-flight sessions at code update time don't get the fix — they experience
   141→the same premature condensation bug that already exists. Only sessions started after the
   142→update benefit from phase tracking.
   143→
   144→---
   145→

   147→
   148→```

   150→  → Tasks 1 + 2 + 3, with exhaustive unit tests

   175→no git operations. Just `(currentPhase, event) → (newPhase, actions)`.

   181→**Types in `session/phase.go`:**
   182→```go
   183→package session
   184→
   185→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
   186→type Phase string
   187→
   188→const (
   189→    PhaseActive          Phase = "active"
   190→    PhaseActiveCommitted Phase = "active_committed"
   191→    PhaseIdle            Phase = "idle"
   192→    PhaseEnded           Phase = "ended"
   193→)
   194→
   195→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty as PhaseIdle
   196→// for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
   197→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
   198→    switch Phase(s) {
   199→    case PhaseActive, PhaseActiveCommitted, PhaseIdle, PhaseEnded:
   200→        return Phase(s)
   201→    default:
   202→        return PhaseIdle // empty or unknown → idle (backward compat)
   203→    }
   204→}
   205→
   206→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
   207→    return p == PhaseActive || p == PhaseActiveCommitted
   208→}
   209→
   210→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
   211→type Event int
   212→
   213→const (
   214→    EventUserPromptSubmit Event = iota // Agent received a new user prompt
   215→    EventStop                          // Agent turn ended (Stop hook)
   216→    EventGitCommit                     // A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
   217→    EventSessionStart                  // Session process started (SessionStart hook)
   218→    EventSessionStop                   // Session process ended (SessionStop hook)
   219→)
   220→
   221→// Action represents a side effect that should be performed after a transition.
   222→// The caller is responsible for executing these — the state machine only declares them.
   223→type Action int
   224→
   225→const (
   226→    ActionCondense              Action = iota // Condense session data to permanent storage
   227→    ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched              // Condense only if FilesTouched is non-empty
   228→    ActionDiscardIfNoFiles                    // Discard session if FilesTouched is empty

   233→)

    58→
    59→	// LastCheckpointID is the checkpoint ID from last condensation, reused for subsequent commits without new content
    60→	LastCheckpointID id.CheckpointID `json:"last_checkpoint_id,omitempty"`
    61→
    62→	// AgentType identifies the agent that created this session (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI", "Cursor")
    63→	AgentType agent.AgentType `json:"agent_type,omitempty"`
    64→
    65→	// Token usage tracking (accumulated across all checkpoints in this session)
    66→	TokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage `json:"token_usage,omitempty"`
    67→
    68→	// Transcript position when session started (for multi-session checkpoints)
    69→	TranscriptLinesAtStart      int    `json:"transcript_lines_at_start,omitempty"`
    70→	TranscriptIdentifierAtStart string `json:"transcript_identifier_at_start,omitempty"`
    71→
    72→	// TranscriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection)
    73→	TranscriptPath string `json:"transcript_path,omitempty"`
    74→
    75→	// PromptAttributions tracks user and agent line changes at each prompt start.
    76→	// This enables accurate attribution by capturing user edits between checkpoints.
    77→	PromptAttributions []PromptAttribution `json:"prompt_attributions,omitempty"`
    78→
    79→	// PendingPromptAttribution holds attribution calculated at prompt start (before agent runs).
    80→	// This is moved to PromptAttributions when SaveChanges is called.
    81→	PendingPromptAttribution *PromptAttribution `json:"pending_prompt_attribution,omitempty"`
    82→}
    83→
    84→// PromptAttribution captures line-level attribution data at the start of each prompt.
    85→// By recording what changed since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent works,
    86→// we can accurately separate user edits from agent contributions.
    87→type PromptAttribution struct {
    88→	// CheckpointNumber is which checkpoint this was recorded before (1-indexed)
    89→	CheckpointNumber int `json:"checkpoint_number"`
    90→
    91→	// UserLinesAdded is lines added by user since the last checkpoint
    92→	UserLinesAdded int `json:"user_lines_added"`
    93→
    94→	// UserLinesRemoved is lines removed by user since the last checkpoint
    95→	UserLinesRemoved int `json:"user_lines_removed"`
    96→
    97→	// AgentLinesAdded is total agent lines added so far (base → last checkpoint).
    98→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
    99→	AgentLinesAdded int `json:"agent_lines_added"`
   100→
   101→	// AgentLinesRemoved is total agent lines removed so far (base → last checkpoint).
   102→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
   103→	AgentLinesRemoved int `json:"agent_lines_removed"`
   104→
   105→	// UserAddedPerFile tracks per-file user additions for accurate modification tracking.
   106→	// This enables distinguishing user self-modifications from agent modifications.
   107→	// See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details.
   108→	UserAddedPerFile map[string]int `json:"user_added_per_file,omitempty"`
   109→}
   110→
   111→// StateStore provides low-level operations for managing session state files.
   112→//
   113→// StateStore is a primitive for session state persistence. It is NOT the same as
   114→// the Sessions interface - it only handles state files in .git/entire-sessions/,
   115→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.
   116→//
   117→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
   118→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.
   119→type StateStore struct {
   120→	// stateDir is the directory where session state files are stored
   121→	stateDir string
   122→}
   123→
   124→// NewStateStore creates a new state store.
   125→// Uses the git common dir to store session state (shared across worktrees).
   126→func NewStateStore() (*StateStore, error) {
   127→	commonDir, err := getGitCommonDir()
   128→	if err != nil {
   129→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   130→	}
   131→	return &StateStore{
   132→		stateDir: filepath.Join(commonDir, sessionStateDirName),
   133→	}, nil
   134→}
   135→
   136→// NewStateStoreWithDir creates a new state store with a custom directory.
   137→// This is useful for testing.
   138→func NewStateStoreWithDir(stateDir string) *StateStore {
   139→	return &StateStore{stateDir: stateDir}
   140→}
   141→
   142→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   143→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   144→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   145→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   146→
   147→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   148→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   149→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   150→	}
   151→
   152→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   153→
   154→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   155→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   156→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   157→	}
   158→	if err != nil {
   159→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   160→	}
   161→
   162→	var state State
   163→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   164→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   165→	}
   166→	return &state, nil
   167→}
   168→
   169→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   170→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   171→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   172→
   173→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   174→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   175→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   176→	}
   177→
   178→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   179→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   180→	}
   181→
   182→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   183→	if err != nil {
   184→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   188→
   189→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   190→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   191→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   192→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   193→	}
   194→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   195→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   196→	}
   197→	return nil
   198→}
   199→
   200→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   201→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   202→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   203→
   204→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   205→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   206→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   207→	}
   208→
   209→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   210→
   211→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   212→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   213→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   214→		}
   215→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   216→	}
   217→	return nil
   218→}
   219→
   220→// RemoveAll removes the entire session state directory.
   221→// This is used during uninstall to completely remove all session state.
   222→func (s *StateStore) RemoveAll() error {
   223→	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.stateDir); err != nil {
   224→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state directory: %w", err)
   225→	}
   226→	return nil
   227→}
   228→
   229→// List returns all session states.
   230→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   231→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   232→
   233→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   234→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   235→		return nil, nil
   236→	}
   237→	if err != nil {
   238→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	var states []*State
   242→	for _, entry := range entries {
   243→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   244→			continue
   245→		}
   246→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   247→			continue // Skip temp files
   248→		}
   249→
   250→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   251→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   252→		if err != nil {
   253→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   254→		}
   255→		if state == nil {
   256→			continue
   257→		}
   258→
   259→		states = append(states, state)
   260→	}
   261→	return states, nil
   262→}
   263→
   264→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   265→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   266→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   267→}
   268→
   269→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   270→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   271→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   272→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   273→	ctx := context.Background()
   274→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   275→	cmd.Dir = "."
   276→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   277→	if err != nil {
   278→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   282→
   283→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   284→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   285→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   286→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   287→	}
   288→
   289→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   290→}
   291→

    49→// PromptAttribution captures line-level attribution data at the start of each prompt,
    50→// calculated BEFORE the agent runs. This allows us to separate user edits (made between
    51→// prompts) from agent edits (made during prompt execution).
    52→//
    53→// Fields:
    54→//   - CheckpointNumber: Which checkpoint this attribution is for (1-indexed)
    55→//   - UserLinesAdded/Removed: User edits since the last checkpoint (lastCheckpoint → worktree)
    56→//   - AgentLinesAdded/Removed: Cumulative agent work so far (base → lastCheckpoint)
    57→//   - UserAddedPerFile: Per-file breakdown of user additions (for accurate modification tracking)
    58→//
    59→// Note: For checkpoint 1, AgentLinesAdded/Removed are always 0 because there is no previous
    60→// checkpoint to compare against. This doesn't mean the agent hasn't done work yet - it means
    61→// we can't measure cumulative agent work until after the first checkpoint is created.
    62→// These fields become meaningful starting from checkpoint 2.
    63→//
    64→// UserAddedPerFile enables accurate tracking of user self-modifications. When a user modifies
    65→// their own previously-added lines (not agent lines), we shouldn't subtract from the agent's
    66→// contribution. See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details.
    67→type PromptAttribution struct {
    68→	CheckpointNumber  int            `json:"checkpoint_number"`
    69→	UserLinesAdded    int            `json:"user_lines_added"`
    70→	UserLinesRemoved  int            `json:"user_lines_removed"`
    71→	AgentLinesAdded   int            `json:"agent_lines_added"`             // Always 0 for checkpoint 1 (no previous checkpoint)
    72→	AgentLinesRemoved int            `json:"agent_lines_removed"`           // Always 0 for checkpoint 1 (no previous checkpoint)
    73→	UserAddedPerFile  map[string]int `json:"user_added_per_file,omitempty"` // Per-file user additions for modification tracking
    74→}

    80→	SessionID        string          `json:"session_id"`
